confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from four web searches. One returned the RBA rate, and three returned Lisbon price pages: Numbeo data via Expatica (June 2026), Expatistan, and travel guides. Those pages gave a 0.5 L draught beer at about €3.1, a cappuccino at €2.4–2.7, an inexpensive meal at €13.5–15, and a three-course meal for two at about €52. I converted euros to USD with an assumed EUR/USD rate of roughly 1.16 from general knowledge, which I did not look up. Cocktails (€9–12 in central bars) and wine (€4–7 per glass) rest on thinner sources, mostly travel blogs, and I cross-checked them against the beer price. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates for July peak season. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any booking pages. Hostel and hotel prices are the least certain anchors because July rates vary widely by neighbourhood and booking date.
comparable_city_reasoning: Lisbon is priced against its own Numbeo, Expatistan and guide data. It sits below Western European capitals for food and drink and well below them for restaurant meals, but accommodation in July peak season is higher than the food prices suggest. Comparable cities are Porto (slightly cheaper) and Barcelona (similar to slightly higher).
